title: Suspense
paragraphs: CBS's landmark thriller anthology, presenting murder, psychological suspense, crime, horror, and the supernatural with major radio and Hollywood performers in standalone dramatic stories.
CBS mystery/thriller anthology known as radio’s outstanding theater of thrills.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: CBS anthology run (June 17, 1942 to September 30, 1962) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] and William N. Robson Hollywood era (November 4, 1956 to August 23, 1959) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include William N. Robson (producer, director, and host), George Walsh (announcer), Jack Kruschen (performer), Joe DeSantis (performer), Ellen Morgan (performer), Barney Phillips (performer), and Sam Pierce (performer, writer, and radio adaptor).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] and [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]].

The stories often return to murder and violent crime, madness and psychological instability, isolation and entrapment, war and military conflict, science and speculative danger, and deception and hidden identity.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Celebrity-driven dramatic anthology, Literary and original-story adaptation tradition, and Late Golden Age network drama.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|escape|Escape]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|cbs-radio-workshop|CBS Radio Workshop]], and [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]].
